title: Keyboard Message
description: Each button press makes the Leonardo type a message on your computer.

steps.clip: You need: an Arduino Leonardo and its USB cable, a breadboard, 1 × pushbutton, 1 × 10 kΩ resistor, and some jumper wires.
Push the button in across the middle gap: two legs above the gap, two below.
hints: The two legs in one column (above and below the gap) are always joined inside the button.
Pressing joins the left column to the right column.
steps.goal: Put the button across the middle gap.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the button's left column (top half) to pin 4 on the Arduino.
hints: Any hole in that column works.
Pin 4 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.
steps.goal: Connect one side of the button to pin 4.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's 5V pin → the red + row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. The button's right column (bottom half) → that same row.
hints: When you press, 5V flows through the button to the pin.
steps.goal: Connect the other side of the button to 5V.

steps.clip: Push a 10 kΩ resistor in: one leg in the button's left column (bottom half), the other leg in an empty column.
hints: This is a pull-down: it keeps the pin LOW until you press.
Without it the pin 'floats' and reads random values.
steps.goal: Put a 10 kΩ resistor on the button's pin side.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's GND pin → the blue − row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. The 10 kΩ resistor's other leg → that same row.
hints: Now the pin reads LOW, and HIGH only while you press.
steps.goal: Connect the pull-down resistor to GND.

steps.clip: Copy the code into the Arduino IDE and click Upload. Open a text editor, click in it, and press the button: the Leonardo types the message.
